messages:
IncidentBot: PagerDuty alert fired: service=inference-p99-alerts-prod · rule=p99_latency_slo · threshold=1.2s · observed=2.34s · SLO burn=12.4% · region=us-west-2 · link=https://redwood/runbooks/p99_latency
PagerDuty: INC-2026-345 created and paged oncall-latency (severity=high). Escalation policy engaged.
Maya (oncall): ack. I'm on it — joining dashboard now, will collect scope.
Raj: ack. I'll pull sidecar and autoscaler logs for us-west-2.
Maya (oncall): quick snapshot: p95 baseline ~250ms, p99 jumped to 2.3s around 03:22:40 UTC. Error rates are flat, but tail latency spike correlates with a big increase in cache misses on the embedder KV store.
Oliver: any deploys in the last hour? Canary pushed at 03:10 but rollout flagged healthy.
Sophie: no config flips on the control plane. I do see a KV eviction count spike starting 03:21:xx — looks like an eviction/rehydration wave hitting sidecars.
Maya (oncall): that could explain long tail: cache miss -> full model warm -> higher token latencies. For immediate mitigation: reduce batch size, and temporarily disable fallback routing so requests don't pile onto a single hot variant.
Raj: running a safe change:
```
infractl update-pool --pool inference-prod-usw2 --set batch_size=4 --reason "emergency p99 mitigation"
```
Will monitor autoscaler after change.
Sophie: also toggling fallback: `redwoodctl routing set --service inference --fallback=false` (will only affect new requests).
Maya (oncall): applied both actions. Observing metrics...
(1m) Maya (oncall): p99 down to ~1.05s now in us-west-2 — below threshold but SLO burn window still active. p95 unchanged. :white_check_mark:
PagerDuty: INC-2026-345 status -> acknowledged, escalation paused.
Oliver: nice. Can we also clear a small hot-prefix in the KV store to reduce cache churn? Sophie, can you evict safely?
Sophie: Plan: evict prefix `embedder:recent-requests` on a rolling basis to avoid stampede. Command queued: `kvctl evict --prefix embedder:recent-requests --region us-west-2 --rolling 5m`
Maya (oncall): go for it.
(5m) Raj: autoscaler metrics stable, CPU/GPU healthy, no OOMs. KV eviction started, miss rate trending down.
(10m) Maya (oncall): p99 holding ~0.9-1.1s, SLO burn dropping. Customer impact: partial degradation for text-gen endpoints in us-west-2 between 03:21-03:29 UTC; some client retries observed but no widespread errors.
Sophie: incident ticket INC-2026-345 updated with mitigation steps and immediate root-cause hypothesis: eviction wave due to TTL and a burst of unique prefixes.
Maya (oncall): handoff plan — I'll monitor for 30m, then hand to Raj for a further 2h watch. If p99 jumps back above 1.2s, escalate to SRE-Infra and open a hotfix for KV TTL defaults.
Raj: taking after-handoff at 04:00 UTC. I'll keep an eye on eviction rate and consider scaling the embedder pool by +2 if we see repeat waves.
Oliver: I'll own the postmortem and follow up on long-term fixes: better prefix cardinality controls, adaptive TTL, and routing backpressure for fallback variants.
Next Oncall: handoff accepted. leaving monitoring window open. :eyes:
IncidentBot: INC-2026-345 status -> monitoring. Assignees: Oliver (postmortem), Raj (follow-up on autoscale/watch).
Maya (oncall): final note — no rollback required, no customer-facing outage escalations. Will add logs and graphs to the incident ticket and assign priority for RCA. Thanks everyone. :zap:
